terms.gloss: torture, torment, in body or mind; crucior, I am in torment
evidence: Plaut. Capt. 600: Crucior, lapidem nōn habēre mē
Cic. Fin. 2.65: cum vigiliīs et famē cruciārētur (Lewis & Short)
Plaut. Mil. 3.2.45: excruciābit mē erus (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: tear with torment; discrucior animī, I am in anguish
terms.register: vōx cōmica: Plaut.; Cic. in epistulīs
evidence: Plaut. Aul. 105: discrucior animī, quia ab domō abeundum est mihi
terms.comment: Repeatedly in Plautus and Cicero, elsewhere rare (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: Crucior, lapidem nōn habēre mē, ut illī mastīgiae cerebrum excutiam.
phrases.english: It torments me that I haven’t a stone, to knock that scoundrel’s brains out.

phrases.latin: discrucior animī, quia ab domō abeundum est mihi
phrases.english: I am in anguish, because I have to leave the house

sources: Lewis & Short: crucio · Lewis & Short: excrucio · Lewis & Short: discrucio
